safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with breathlessness for 2–3 days.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts list SOB/wheeze/cough but do not state the duration of breathlessness (2–3 days).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting the 2–3 day duration of breathlessness reduces the ability to judge acuity and trajectory of the episode, which can influence assessment of exacerbation severity and urgency of review. This can lead to suboptimal triage or delayed escalation if symptoms are actually rapidly evolving.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has experienced breathlessness for 2–3 days.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No duration of symptoms (2–3 days) is captured in the generated HPI.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting symptom duration in the HPI impairs clinical interpretation of whether this is an acute exacerbation versus a more chronic deterioration, affecting decisions such as same-day assessment versus routine follow-up. The likely impact is additional clarification/monitoring rather than direct injury.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient normally uses the blue inhaler only as needed.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold notes patient normally uses blue inhaler only as needed; generated does not explicitly state the baseline pattern (PRN-only when well).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Baseline reliever (blue inhaler) use being PRN-only when well is important context for identifying increased reliever reliance, a key marker of poor control/exacerbation severity. Without this, the record may underestimate change-from-baseline and affect step-up decisions and safety-netting intensity.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient is taking the Clenil inhaler every day, 2 puffs twice daily.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes 'Clenil (daily)' but does not include the baseline dose/frequency '2 puffs twice daily'.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not capturing the regular Clenil dose (2 puffs twice daily) removes the reference point needed to safely and accurately “step up” inhaled steroid dosing during worsening symptoms. This can cause dosing ambiguity and may result in inappropriate escalation/de-escalation or extra follow-up to reconcile the regimen.
